_doc: Inputs of RunnerBalance, the economy + power model behind the runner's 50-level curve (tests/Survival.Domain.Tests/RunnerBalanceTests.cs, docs/runner_balance.md). Hero stats, level-up gold / food / timers, star caps, shards, runner rewards, campaign stages, bounties, quests, the free gift pool, farm output and the rush rate are read from the real game files. Every number in THIS file is a modelling assumption; the ones marked _invented are placeholders Derek has to confirm (pace, village income, the gem resource crate that does not exist in the store yet).

pace._invented: How a 'normal' free player plays: 3 sessions a day, each session tries the next runner level once and replays the best cleared level once (a modest replay count); the timeline stops after max_days.

village._invented: Free income outside the runner: farms (count and level assumed; output and capacity per level come from base_economy.json), how often the player collects them, how many of the 6 daily free gifts he opens, and the share of gold he puts into heroes (the rest goes on buildings). Campaign stages 1-6 and the bounties are assumed cleared one per day from day 1; the starter quests on day 1.

gems._source: sku.hard_m: 500 gems for $4.99 (store pack products.json / stores.json offer.gems_m).
gems._invented_crate: The only thing gems buy for heroes today is rush time (1 gem / minute) and hero unlocks; there is no gem -> gold / food offer. The model assumes a 'resource crate' offer: 100 gems -> 30000 gold + 15000 food. Without some such offer a payer cannot outpace the gold / food cost of training and the late wall is a wall for everyone.

greedy._doc: Best power per cost: cost = gold + food_value * food.
